markets.title: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than expected, complicating Fed's inflation fight
markets.raw_summary: The report comes at a critical juncture for the Federal Reserve as it considers its next move regarding interest rates.

insight.what: 美国10月CPI环比涨0.4%，高于市场预期，说明通胀回落的最后一公里仍不通畅。
insight.why: 市场原本定价12月还会再降一次息；这份数据打掉了「通胀已受控」这个前提，短端美债收益率与美元要重新定价，长久期资产的折现率上修。
insight.chain: CPI环比超预期 → 通胀黏性确认 → 降息预期降温 → 2年期美债收益率上行 → 美元指数走强 → 高估值成长股折现率抬升 → 纳指承压
notes: CPI 是消费者物价指数：单月涨 0.4% 若持续一年，年化接近 5%，远高于美联储 2% 的目标，所以单月超预期也足以改变市场对整条加息路径的预期。
先动的是两年期美债：它的收益率大致等于市场对未来两年政策利率的平均预期——它不反映当下的利率，反映的是大家预期美联储接下来往哪走。
债券价格和收益率反向变动：票息是固定的，市场要求的回报一变，只能靠价格调整来匹配。
股票是同一套折算逻辑：成长股的大部分利润在很远的未来，要求的回报率每上一个台阶，对它们的估值削减得更狠。
美元走强的机制是利差：美国利率相对更高，资金买入美元资产；反过来，新兴市场本币贬值和美元债偿付压力同时上升。

insight_en.what: US October CPI rose 0.4% month on month, above expectations, showing the last mile of disinflation is still sticky.
insight_en.why: Markets had priced one more Fed cut in December. This print removes the premise that inflation is contained, forcing a repricing of front-end Treasuries and the dollar, and lifting the discount rate on long-duration assets.
insight_en.chain: CPI beats forecasts → sticky inflation confirmed → rate-cut odds fall → 2-year Treasury yield rises → dollar index strengthens → growth-stock discount rate climbs → Nasdaq comes under pressure
notes: CPI is the consumer price index: the monthly figure is one month's change, the annual figure compounds twelve. A steady 0.4% a month is roughly 5% annualised, far above the Fed's 2% target, which is why one upside surprise can move the whole path.

Why the 2-year moves first: its yield is roughly the average policy rate expected over the next two years plus a small term premium. It does not price today's rate but where the Fed is expected to go, so it reacts fastest to any change in that expectation.

Bond prices and yields move inversely because the coupon is fixed and the price must adjust until yield-to-maturity equals what the market demands: `P = C/(1+y)¹ + C/(1+y)² + … + (C+Face)/(1+y)ⁿ`. When y rises every denominator grows, so the price must fall; the longer the duration, the bigger the fall.

Equity valuation uses the same discounting logic: `PV = CF₁/(1+r)¹ + CF₂/(1+r)² + …`. Growth companies earn most of their cash flow far in the future, so every step up in r cuts their present value harder than it does for a value stock with near-term cash flows. That is what long-duration equity means.

The dollar channel is a rate differential: when US rates rise relative to others, `i_USD − i_foreign` widens, carry money buys dollar assets, dollar demand rises and the currency appreciates. On the other side, emerging-market currencies weaken and their dollar debt service gets heavier, which drives capital outflows.

Hawkish means more worried about inflation and inclined to tighten; dovish means more worried about growth and jobs. This print makes the Fed less able to be dovish without making it hawkish. The middle ground is the most uncomfortable, because uncertainty itself must be priced, and the way it gets priced is a higher risk premium.

markets.title: France and Belgium fall foul of Eurozone bond market’s new divide
markets.raw_summary: Global sell-off during Iran war has prompted investors to zero in on new group of Eurozone countries facing debt challenges

insight.what: 伊朗战争引发全球债市抛售，投资者把法国、比利时单独拎出来，划入财政脆弱国家的新名单。
insight.why: 市场原本只给意大利、希腊这类老牌高债务国加风险补偿；现在法、比也被归入同一组，两国国债相对德国 Bund 的利差要重新定价，欧元区内部资金开始分层。
insight.chain: 伊朗战争推高能源价格 → 增长与财政双重恶化 → 重估各国债务可持续性 → 法、比被划入脆弱组 → OAT对Bund利差走阔 → 套利资金撤出 → 两国融资成本上升
notes: 主权利差是一国国债收益率减去德国国债收益率：德国债被视为欧元区的无风险基准，其他国家借钱都要多付一笔补偿，这笔补偿就是利差。
利差走阔和财政恶化互为因果：财政越差，市场要求的补偿越高，利息负担越重，财政更差。
债务可持续性看的是利率和增长谁跑得快：借钱的平均利息高于名义增长时，即使不新增赤字，债务占比也会自己往上走。
欧元区的结构性弱点：货币统一、财政分散，没有跨国转移支付——成员国出问题只能自己发债，外部冲击自动变成国别信用风险。
法国比意大利更让市场紧张：它是欧元区第二大经济体、大量基金的基准持仓，一旦被降级，按评级管钱的机构会被动减仓，卖压比小国更大。

insight_en.what: A global bond sell-off triggered by the Iran war has led investors to single out France and Belgium as a new group of fiscally fragile euro members.
insight_en.why: Markets had charged a premium only to the old high-debt names such as Italy and Greece. Now France and Belgium join that bucket, so their spreads to Bund must be repriced and capital starts to stratify inside the euro area.
insight_en.chain: Iran war lifts energy prices → growth and fiscal position worsen → debt sustainability reassessed → France and Belgium classed as fragile → OAT-Bund spread widens → arbitrage capital exits → funding costs rise
notes: Sovereign spread means a country's bond yield minus the German Bund yield. Bunds are treated as the euro area's risk-free benchmark: top rating, deepest market, best liquidity, so every other sovereign pays a compensation on top of it, and that compensation is the spread.

How the spread is computed: `Spread = y_France − y_Germany`. A wider spread means the market demands more compensation, and it also means new issuance costs more. The two feed each other: worse fiscal position, wider spread, heavier interest bill, worse fiscal position.

Debt sustainability is about whether the interest rate outruns growth. When nominal growth g is below the average interest rate r, the debt-to-GDP ratio rises even with no new deficit, roughly `Δ(D/Y) ≈ (r − g) × (D/Y) − primary surplus`. The gap between r and g is the core variable.

The structural weakness of the euro area: one currency, many fiscal authorities, no cross-border fiscal transfer. A US state in trouble is backstopped by the federal budget; a euro member in trouble issues its own debt, so the same external shock automatically becomes country credit risk.

Why France worries markets more than Italy: it is the second-largest euro economy, rated in the AA band, and OATs are benchmark holdings for many funds and insurers. A downgrade or a wider spread forces rating- and duration-constrained managers to sell, and that forced selling is far bigger than in a smaller market.

How arbitrage capital amplifies the move: carry trades funded in low-yielding currency or repo against high-yielding government bonds get margin calls when the spread gaps, so they sell the bonds at the same time. The price drop is amplified by their own deleveraging, which is what crowded-trade unwinds look like.

Transmission to FX: as the member risk premium rises, euro assets look less attractive, money flows to the dollar and the euro weakens. That is the same event expressed in a second price, just in a market that reacts faster.

policy.title: China’s shipyards overtake South Korea’s in LNG carrier market as demand surges
policy.raw_summary: China has overtaken South Korea in monthly orders for liquefied natural gas (LNG) carriers for the first time, challenging its rival’s long-standing dominance in a high-value shipbuilding segment wher

insight.what: 中国船厂月度接单首次超过韩国：全球7艘大型LNG船订单，中国拿下5艘。
insight.why: 市场原本认为LNG船是韩国最后一块高利润堡垒；份额转移意味着高附加值造船的定价权和订单簿开始向中国倾斜，韩国船企的盈利溢价需要下修。
insight.chain: 中国拿下5艘LNG船订单 → 高附加值订单簿转移 → 韩国船企议价力下降 → 韩国船厂毛利承压 → 中国产能利用率上升 → 配套设备需求上行 → 中韩出口结构此消彼长
notes: LNG 船是运输零下 163 度液化天然气的专用船，核心壁垒在货舱保温系统，能做的船厂很少——单价是普通散货船的四到六倍，是造船业利润最厚的船型。
韩国紧张的原因：LNG 船是韩国三大船企的高毛利支柱，这块份额被切走，等于最赚钱的产品线开始面对价格竞争。
单月接单第一不等于格局反转，但市场定价看的是预期——预期先于报表改变，所以单月数据也足以引发估值调整。
造船是订单驱动、产能刚性的生意：接单后两三年才交船确认收入，今天的订单簿决定的是两三年后的利润，所以造船股总是提前反应。
对中国来说，受益的不只是船厂，还有钢板、船用发动机、导航设备这一整条配套链。

insight_en.what: Chinese yards beat South Korean rivals in monthly orders for the first time: of seven large LNG carrier orders worldwide, China won five.
insight_en.why: Markets had treated LNG carriers as Korea's last high-margin fortress. The share shift means pricing power and order books in high-value shipbuilding are tilting toward China, so Korea's earnings premium needs to be marked down.
insight_en.chain: China wins five LNG orders → high-value order book shifts → Korean pricing power erodes → Korean yard margins compress → Chinese utilisation rises → equipment demand picks up → export mix shifts between them
notes: An LNG carrier hauls natural gas chilled to minus 163 degrees Celsius; the core barrier is the membrane containment system and very few yards can build it. A unit typically costs four to six times a large bulk carrier, which makes it the fattest-margin segment in shipbuilding and Korea's last moat.

Why Korea cares: LNG carriers are the high-margin pillar for its big three yards, HD Hyundai, Samsung Heavy and Hanwha Ocean. Losing share means the most profitable line starts competing on price instead of collecting a technology premium.

How share is computed: `share = national orders ÷ global orders`. Monthly data is noisy and one month at the top is not a regime change, but markets price expectations, and expectations move before the financials do.

Shipbuilding is order-driven with rigid capacity: slipways and docks cannot be added quickly, and an order placed today delivers and books revenue in two to three years. Today's order book sets profits two to three years out, not this quarter, which is why yard stocks react early.

How margin gets squeezed: `gross margin ≈ contract price − build cost`. The contract price is locked at signing while steel prices and the currency keep moving, so the more you book and the longer the lock, the larger the cost exposure. That is why yards chase high-priced orders and avoid cheap ones.

Macro read-through: higher-value exports replacing lower-value ones improves the terms of trade, but it is near-term negative for Korea's trade balance and the won. For China the beneficiaries are not only yards but the whole supply chain: steel plate, marine engines, navigation and automation gear.

policy.title: Spain's first general strike in 14 years demands solutions to housing crisis
policy.raw_summary: Less than three weeks before a national election that could catapult the far right to power, Spain's workers are striking on Wednesday to demand that the government remedy the nation's housing crisis.

insight.what: 西班牙14年来首次全国大罢工，抗议房租与房价；距大选不到三周，极右翼可能上台。
insight.why: 市场原本把西班牙当欧元区财政改善的优等生；罢工与大选不确定性把政治风险溢价重新塞回定价，Bonos相对Bund的利差和IBEX都要重估。
insight.chain: 房租与房价涨幅超收入 → 住房成为选举核心议题 → 全国大罢工施压政府 → 财政补贴承诺加码 → 赤字预期上修 → 极右翼支持率上升 → 西债利差走阔
notes: 大罢工直接压掉当期产出和消费，损失大致等于日均产出乘停工天数乘参与率。
住房危机变成主权信用问题的路径：政府要用补贴、租金管制和公屋投资来回应，这些都要花钱，社会问题一旦需要财政兜底，就进入债券市场的视野。
政治不确定会被计入国债收益率：政治越动荡，投资者要求的补偿越高——收益率里多出来的那部分就是政治溢价。
西班牙之前利差收窄得有多漂亮，怀疑出现时就要还回去多少，而且更快——因为看多的资金要一起平仓。
另一条链走通胀：罢工推高工资诉求，工资传导到服务价格，拖慢欧央行降息节奏——这条链对汇率和短期利率的影响比财政链更快。

insight_en.what: Spain held its first general strike in 14 years over housing costs, less than three weeks before an election that could bring the far right to power.
insight_en.why: Markets had treated Spain as the euro area's fiscal improver. The strike and election uncertainty put a political risk premium back into pricing, forcing a repricing of Bonos spreads to Bund and of the IBEX.
insight_en.chain: Rents outrun incomes → housing becomes the election issue → general strike pressures government → subsidy pledges grow → deficit forecasts revised up → far-right support rises → Spanish spread widens
notes: A general strike is a nationwide, cross-industry stoppage, unlike a strike at one company. It directly subtracts current output and consumption. The short-run loss is roughly `loss ≈ daily output × strike days × participation rate`, usually a few tenths of a percent, so on its own it does not change the macro forecast.

Why a housing crisis becomes a sovereign credit issue: when rents outrun incomes for long enough, the government can only respond with subsidies, rent controls and public housing investment, all of which cost money and land in the deficit and the debt. Once a social problem needs a fiscal backstop, bond markets start pricing it.

Political risk premium decomposes like this: `y_Spain = y_Bund + credit risk + liquidity premium + political premium`. For the same bond, the more political uncertainty, the more compensation investors demand, and the extra yield is the political premium.

Spain has been one of the euro area's fastest growers for two years, with tourism and immigration supporting employment, and its spread had narrowed close to France's. The catch: whatever was compressed has to be given back when doubt returns, and usually faster, because crowded longs unwind together.

The market meaning of a far-right government is not a moral judgement but a fiscal path: if it delivers tax cuts and welfare pledges the deficit widens; if it clashes with EU budget rules, disbursement from the recovery fund slows. Both widen the spread, just at different times.

The second channel runs through inflation: strikes raise wage demands, wages feed service prices, and services are the stickiest part of core inflation, which slows the ECB's easing. This channel hits FX and the front end faster than the fiscal one.

tech.title: Anthropic Aims for $3 Billion to $3.5 Billion in Japan Offering
tech.raw_summary: Anthropic PBC is seeking to raise $3 billion to $3.5 billion from Japanese investors as part of its initial public offering, keeping the fundraising target in the country after the frontier artificial

insight.what: Anthropic启动IPO路演，计划向日本投资者募资30亿至35亿美元。
insight.why: 市场原本把AI资本开支当成巨头用自有现金流就能撑住的故事；前沿实验室转向公开市场融资，AI投入开始依赖外部资本供给，估值锚也从一级市场挪到二级市场。
insight.chain: 前沿AI公司IPO路演 → 日本募资30-35亿美元 → AI融资转向公开市场 → 估值接受二级市场检验 → 日本资金买美股新股 → 日元与日股资金面承压 → 同业AI融资成本被锚定
notes: IPO 是首次公开发行：之前估值由少数风投谈出来，上市之后每天由市场报价，估值从此有了公开参照，也意味着每天都要接受检验。
募资额和估值不是一回事：募 30 亿美元、出让 10% 股份，隐含估值就是 300 亿——看新闻第一件事是分清它说的是融资额还是估值。
在日本募资值得注意：日本长期低利率，本地资金有大量海外配置需求——对 Anthropic 是融资渠道，对日本是资本外流。
跨境认购影响汇率：日本投资者要把日元换成美元申购，日元承压；规模够大时会和日本当局的汇率干预形成对冲。
AI 公司的融资结构正在从「巨头的战略投资」转向公开市场：资金从近乎零成本变成有明确回报要求，同样的 GPU 订单算下来就没那么值了。

insight_en.what: Anthropic has begun marketing its IPO and aims to raise $3bn to $3.5bn from Japanese investors.
insight_en.why: Markets had framed AI capex as something the giants could fund from their own cash flow. A frontier lab turning to public markets means AI spending now depends on external capital, and the valuation anchor moves from private marks to public quotes.
insight_en.chain: Frontier AI firm markets IPO → raises $3-3.5bn in Japan → AI funding shifts to public markets → valuation tested by public investors → Japanese money buys US new issues → yen and local liquidity pressured → peers' cost of capital anchored
notes: An IPO is an initial public offering: the company sells shares to public investors and lists on an exchange. Before that it raised private capital, with valuation negotiated by a handful of VCs; after listing it is quoted daily, so the valuation gains a public reference and a daily exam.

Fundraising size and valuation are different things: `valuation = amount raised ÷ percentage of shares sold`. Raise $3bn for 10% of the company and the implied valuation is $30bn. The first thing to check in any IPO story is which of the two is being quoted, because they differ by an order of magnitude.

Why raising in Japan matters: Japanese households and institutions have large offshore allocation needs, and years of low local rates make them willing to buy dollar assets for yield. For Anthropic it is a funding channel, for Japan it is capital outflow, for the world it is one more pool of money chasing AI assets.

FX effect of cross-border subscription: Japanese investors must sell yen to buy dollars for the deal, so `yen supply rises and dollar demand rises`, and the yen weakens. At a large enough size this offsets official intervention, which is why big offshore deals get watched by FX desks.

The funding structure of AI is changing: from operating cash flow and strategic cheques from giants toward equity and debt markets. The cost of capital moves from near-zero strategic money to public money with explicit return demands, so the net present value of the same GPU order falls, because the discount rate rose.

A lockup is the period after listing during which existing shareholders cannot sell, typically 180 days. When it expires, share supply jumps, and if fundamentals have not improved in step, selling arrives all at once. That is the technical, not emotional, reason people worry this IPO cycle marks a turning point for the AI trade.

tech.title: Malaysia to Start Electricity Market for Data Center Operators
tech.raw_summary: Malaysia intends to launch a separate wholesale electricity market for large power consumers including data centers, the New Straits Times reported.

insight.what: 马来西亚计划为数据中心等大用电户单设批发电力市场，让电价由专门市场出清决定。
insight.why: 市场原本把东南亚数据中心的瓶颈算在芯片、土地和审批上；电力变成可交易、可定价的稀缺资源，数据中心的边际成本曲线被重画，选址与资本开支节奏随之改变。
insight.chain: 数据中心用电激增 → 电网容量成为瓶颈 → 马来西亚设电力市场 → 大用户电价市场出清 → 电价上行且更波动 → 数据中心运营成本上升 → 算力扩张节奏放缓
notes: 批发电力市场是把电当商品集中交易：多数市场由最贵的那台机组决定全网电价——它一进来，所有买家的结算价都被抬高。
数据中心是电老虎，一座大型园区用电量相当于几十万户家庭；行业用「电能利用效率」衡量浪费，越接近 1 越省电，热带地区天然吃亏。
单独设市场的原因：让用得多的人付得多，把电网扩容的成本和电力的稀缺性显性化，而不是让居民和大用户互相补贴。
电费对投资决策的杀伤力大于一次性建造成本：电费是运营期每年都发生的支出，电价一涨，原本算得过来的项目就变得不划算。
马来西亚承接了大量从新加坡外溢的数据中心需求——这次单设市场，等于官方承认电力已是招商引资的核心筹码。

insight_en.what: Malaysia plans a separate wholesale electricity market for large users such as data centres, letting a dedicated market clear the price.
insight_en.why: Markets had counted Southeast Asian data-centre bottlenecks in chips, land and permits. Power is becoming a tradable, priced scarce input, which redraws the marginal cost curve and changes siting and capex timing.
insight_en.chain: Data-centre demand surges → grid capacity becomes the bottleneck → Malaysia creates a power market → large-user tariffs clear by market → prices rise and get volatile → operating costs climb → compute build-out slows
notes: A wholesale power market is where electricity is traded as a commodity and the price clears supply against demand. Most use marginal pricing: the last plant needed to meet demand sets the price for everyone, so when the expensive unit switches on, every buyer's settlement price rises with it.

Data centres are power hogs: one large campus can draw as much as hundreds of thousands of homes. The industry measures waste with PUE, power usage effectiveness, `total power = IT load × PUE`. The closer PUE is to 1 the more efficient; tropical sites run higher because cooling load is heavy.

Why a separate market: if data centres and households share one tariff, either households subsidise the large user or the large user pushes peak costs onto households. Carving out a dedicated market makes grid expansion costs and power scarcity explicit, so heavy users pay for what they take.

How power costs enter the investment case: `NPV = Σ (revenue − power cost)/(1+r)ᵗ − capex`. Power is a cash outflow every year of operation, so it damages NPV far more than a one-off build cost; when tariffs rise, projects that pencilled out can flip negative.

This changes the pace of compute expansion: a delivered GPU is not a running GPU, and grid connection queues plus substation construction are measured in years. Once power is a hard constraint, the lag between chip orders and live compute lengthens, which is the real-world version of buying cards with no power to run them.

Malaysia's position: Johor sits next to Singapore and absorbs much of the data-centre demand spilling out of it, because Singapore is short of both land and power. Creating a dedicated market is an official admission that power is now the core selling point for attracting investment, not a utility afterthought.

Second-order effect on asset prices: higher power costs lift data-centre capitalisation rates, and `value = net operating income ÷ cap rate`. A bigger denominator means a lower value, which is the most direct exposure for data-centre REITs and infrastructure funds, and it moves faster than rents do.
